02 · Safety & Scope
Before you begin
What InnerSoothe
is — and isn't
Please read this before continuing. It takes 30 seconds.
✅ InnerSoothe IS
A self-help wellness app with evidence-based techniques
Drawn from CBT, ACT, Narrative Therapy and clinical hypnotherapy frameworks
A private, personal space to process emotions at your own pace
Designed with input from qualified psychologists
❌ InnerSoothe is NOT
A substitute for professional therapy or counselling
A crisis intervention or emergency service
A medical tool — it does not diagnose or treat any condition
Intended for use during acute mental health crises
💡 Who this is for
InnerSoothe is for adults navigating the pain of a breakup or relationship loss who want structured, evidence-based tools to support their healing journey.
🆘 If you need crisis support
🇮🇳 India — iCall 9152987821
🇺🇸 US — 988 Lifeline Call / Text 988
🇬🇧 UK — Samaritans 116 123
🇦🇺 Australia — Lifeline 13 11 14
If you are in crisis, please reach out to a service above before continuing.
Regulatory positioning: This screen establishes "wellness tool" not "medical device" — critical for MHRA, TGA and FDA classification. Required by Apple App Store mental health guidelines.
03 · Consent & Privacy
Your privacy matters
How we handle
your data
Plain English. No legal walls. You're in control.
📥 What we collect
•Your emotion check-ins and session progress
•Account email and name
•Device type and anonymous usage patterns
🚫 What we NEVER collect
•Journal entries (stored only on your device)
•Your therapy session content or responses
•Location data, contacts or photos
•Your data is never sold — ever
🔒 Your rights (GDPR / DPDP)
•Export all your data anytime from Settings
•Delete your account and all data permanently
•Withdraw consent at any time

Why This Flow Works
Every decision backed by onboarding research

Value before account

Quick win on screen 4

"Just starting 🌱" → "Almost there ✨" → "You're in 🎉". Goal gradient effect drives completion.

Your Insight Report
Based on today · 3 emotions logged
Your emotional state today
Grieving under pressure
Unresolved loss, blocked momentum, and sustained anxiety — your nervous system is carrying more than it should right now.
Why these emotions co-occur
When grief and anxiety operate simultaneously, the nervous system enters a freeze-flight conflict — wanting to withdraw and escape at once. Frustration signals that neither need is being met.
🫀
Where you may feel this
Chest heaviness, shallow breath, tension behind the eyes. Possibly a hollow feeling in the stomach.

Full Session · 5 minutes
9:41●●●
✦ GUIDED SESSION · HYPNODRAMA
PROCESS THE RELATIONSHIP
The Healing Conversation
A guided hypnotherapy session where you meet the person in a safe imagined space, say everything that needs to be said, and find your own insight for healing.
‹
Design Comparison
Single Screen vs Multi Screen
🎭 Hypnodrama — Single Screen
One continuous visual journey. The SVG evolves through 7 phases: breath → countdown → mist → two figures → conversation energy → release → golden insight → dots.

Simpler UX — user just watches and listens. No navigation required during the session.
✂️ Cord Cutting — 5 Screens
Five distinct scenes with unique visuals per phase. User navigates with Next/Previous. Each screen has dedicated animations.

Richer visual narrative — each phase feels distinct and intentional.
📋 For Psychologist Review
Which approach feels more therapeutically appropriate for a 5-minute hypnodrama session?

Key question: Should the user actively navigate between phases, or should the experience be fully passive (single screen)?

Step 1 · Ground & Settle
9:41●●●
← Paid Techniques
🪑 Empty Chair
Step 1 of 8
Step 1 of 8 · Ground & Settle
Arrive in your body before anything else.
Before we begin, we need to drop out of the thinking mind and into the feeling body. This exercise works only when you're present — not rehearsing.
DO THIS NOW
Place both feet flat on the floor. Feel the weight of your body in your chair. Take three slow breaths — in through the nose, out through the mouth. With each exhale, let your shoulders drop a little more.

Step 2 · Choose Who Sits Opposite
9:41●●●
← Paid Techniques
🪑 Empty Chair
Step 2 of 8
Step 2 of 8 · Set the Stage
Who needs to be in that chair?
The empty chair holds whoever you have unfinished business with. This could be someone who hurt you, someone you've lost, a younger version of yourself, or even a feeling like shame or grief.
WHO IS IT?
Close your eyes. Picture them sitting in the chair across from you. Don't force it — let whoever shows up, show up. Notice what you feel in your body as you imagine them there.

Step 1 of 8 · Ground & Arrive
Create safety before you go inward.
Inner child work asks you to visit old pain. You need to feel safe in your adult body first — so that young part of you knows they are being visited by someone who can actually help.
DO THIS NOW
Find a quiet place. Sit with your back supported. Place one hand on your chest, one on your belly. Take five slow breaths — feel both hands rise and fall. With each exhale, say silently: 'I am safe. I am an adult. I can handle what I find.'

ASK YOURSELF
Close your eyes. Think about the feeling at the core of your current pain — the one underneath the sadness. Maybe it's 'I am unlovable.' Or 'People always leave.' Or 'I am too much.' Now ask: how old was I the first time I felt this? Let a number or an image arise. Don't force it.
There is no wrong answer. Whatever age appears — that is the one that needs you.

🔊 Guided · Intro — What is Cognitive Defusion?
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
ACT · Free · ~15 min
Your thoughts are not facts.
You don't have to believe everything you think.
After a breakup, the mind generates a flood of painful thoughts. "I'll never find love again." "I am too much." "They were the only one." These thoughts feel like truth. They are not.
WHAT IS COGNITIVE DEFUSION?
Defusion is an ACT technique. It creates psychological distance between you and your thoughts — so you can observe them without being controlled by them. You learn to see thoughts as events in the mind, not facts about reality.
In this session you will:
🎯
Identify the thought
What is the painful story your mind keeps telling?
👁️
Label it as a thought
"I am having the thought that I am unlovable"
🌊
Watch it without merging
Thoughts as clouds passing — you are the sky
🌿
Choose your response
Act from values, not from the thought
🌸Check-In
🌿Heal
📖Journal
📊Progress

🔊 Guided · Step 1 — Identify the Thought
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
Step 1 of 5 · Identify
What is the thought your mind keeps coming back to?
There is usually one core painful thought underneath the breakup grief. Not the story — the core belief. It often sounds like: "I am not enough." "People always leave me." "I am unlovable."
PAUSE AND NOTICE
Right now, close your eyes for 30 seconds. Don't try to stop thoughts — just watch what comes. What is the most painful thought that keeps appearing? What is your mind most convinced is true about you or your future?
The thought I keep having is...
"I am not enough — that's why they left."
This is an example. Your thought will be specific to you. Take a moment to find the real one before you continue.

🔊 Guided · Step 2 — Fusion vs Defusion
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
Step 2 of 5 · Understand the Difference
Fused with a thought vs. seeing a thought.
When you are fused with a thought, you live inside it — it becomes reality. Defusion creates space. Same thought, completely different relationship to it.
⚠ Fused
"I am unlovable."

This feels like a fact. You search for evidence. You act from it. It shrinks your world.
✓ Defused
"I notice I'm having the thought that I am unlovable."

Same thought. Now you can see it. You are not it.
THE SHIFT
Notice how adding 'I notice I am having the thought that...' changes everything. It's not denial. The thought is still there. But now you are the observer of the thought — not the thought itself.

I understand the difference between being fused and defused

🔊 Guided · Step 3 — Apply Defusion
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
Step 3 of 5 · Apply
Pick one technique. Apply it to your thought right now.
Take the core thought you identified. Now run it through one of these defusion techniques. Actually do it — say it aloud or write it down.
🏷️
Label it
"I am having the thought that I am not enough." — Puts distance between you and the thought immediately.
🧠
Thank your mind
"Thank you, mind, for this thought. I see it." — Treats the mind with gentle humour, not war.
🌊
Clouds passing
Visualise the thought written on a cloud, floating past. You are the sky — vast, unchanging, watching.
🎵
Sing it
Sing your painful thought to "Happy Birthday." It sounds absurd — which reveals it is just sounds, not truth.

← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
Step 4 of 5 · Observe
You are not your thoughts.
You are the one noticing them.
This is the deepest part of defusion. The noticing mind — the part of you reading this right now — is always separate from the thoughts being noticed. It cannot be defined or damaged by them.
DO THIS NOW
Close your eyes. Notice a thought arise. Any thought. Now notice the part of you that is noticing the thought. That noticing awareness has been with you your whole life — through every thought, every emotion, every experience. It is untouched. It is you.
The thought "I am unlovable" arises in awareness. But the awareness itself is never unlovable. It is simply here — clear, present, whole.

🔊 Guided · Step 5 — Act from Values, Not Thoughts
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🌀Cognitive Defusion · ACT · Free
Cognitive Defusion
Step 5 of 5 · Choose
The thought can be there. You still get to choose.
Defusion is not about eliminating thoughts — they will keep coming. It is about creating enough space between you and the thought that you can choose a response that aligns with your values rather than the thought's agenda.
ASK YOURSELF
"If I act from this thought — what does my life look like? If I act from my values instead — what becomes possible? What does the person I want to be do next, whether this thought is here or not?"
The thought "I am unlovable" can be present — and you can still reach out to a friend, take care of your body, choose healing. That is defusion in action.
✓
I know the one thing I'll do next, regardless of this thought

🧠Cognitive Distortions · CBT · Free
Cognitive Distortions
CBT · Free · ~20 min
Your mind is running thinking traps.
This session helps you name them.
After a breakup, the mind becomes flooded with distorted thinking — patterns that feel like truth but are not. CBT calls these cognitive distortions. When you can name one, it loses some of its power over you.
What you'll do:
1. Learn the 10 most common distortions
2. Identify which ones you're living inside
3. Examine one closely
4. Write a more balanced thought
You don't need to eliminate these thoughts. You just need to see them for what they are — patterns, not facts.

📦 Intro — What is the Container Box?
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
📦Container Box · DBT · Free
Container Box
DBT · Free · ~10 min
Pain doesn't have to flood you all day.
You can choose when to feel it.
The Container Box is a DBT visualisation technique. You create a mental container — a box — and temporarily place painful thoughts, feelings, and images inside it. You close the lid. The pain stays contained until you choose to open it.
This is not avoidance.
You are not pretending the pain isn't real. You are choosing when to feel it — not at 2am when you can't sleep, not in the middle of a work meeting. You are the one in control.
It works because your nervous system responds to visualisation as if it were real. A well-imagined container genuinely reduces flooding.

🔨 Step 1 — Design your container

📦Container Box · DBT · Free
Container Box
Step 1 of 4 · Build Your Container
Close your eyes. Build a box in your mind.
Visualise a container that feels strong enough to hold your pain. There are no wrong answers — only what works for you.
📏
Size — Big enough to hold everything. A chest, a vault, a steel container, a safe.
🧱
Material — Whatever feels strong. Steel, oak, stone, reinforced glass.
🔒
Lock — A lock only you can open. A combination, a key, a fingerprint.
📍
Location — Where is it? Deep underground, in a sealed room, at the bottom of the ocean.
Take 60 seconds now to actually close your eyes and build this container. The more specific and vivid, the more effective it will be.

💛 Intro — What is Self Compassion?
9:41●●●

💛Self Compassion · MSC · Free
Self Compassion
MSC · Free · ~15 min
You would never speak to a friend the way you speak to yourself.
This session changes that.
Self compassion is not self pity. It is not weakness. Research by Dr Kristin Neff shows it is one of the most powerful predictors of emotional resilience — more effective than self-esteem.
🧠
Mindfulness
Acknowledging the pain without over-identifying with it. "This hurts" — not "I am broken."
🌍
Common Humanity
Recognising that suffering is part of being human — you are not uniquely flawed or alone.
💛
Self-Kindness
Treating yourself with the same warmth you would offer a good friend going through this.

🧠 Step 1 — Acknowledge the pain honestly
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
💛Self Compassion · MSC · Free
Self Compassion
Step 1 of 5 · Mindfulness
Name what is happening.
Don't minimise it. Don't spiral.
Mindfulness means seeing your experience clearly — without suppressing it and without being swept away by it. The first act of self compassion is honest acknowledgement.
Say this to yourself, slowly:
"This is a moment of suffering. This hurts. I am not okay right now — and that is okay."
Then notice:
"Where do I feel this in my body? What does it actually feel like right now — not the story, just the sensation?"
Take 60 seconds. Close your eyes. Say the first phrase aloud. Feel the difference between "I'm fine" and honest acknowledgement.

🌍 Step 2 — You are not alone in this
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
💛Self Compassion · MSC · Free
Self Compassion
Step 2 of 5 · Common Humanity
Every person who has ever loved has also lost.
You are not uniquely broken.
One of the cruelest tricks of suffering is isolation — the feeling that no one else could possibly understand, that you are uniquely flawed for hurting this much. This is not true.
💔
Billions of people are going through heartbreak right now. Not like yours — but real, and painful, and real.
😔
The self-criticism, the replaying, the wondering what you could have done — these are universal human responses to loss.
🌱
The fact that you loved deeply enough to hurt this much is not a weakness. It is evidence of your capacity for connection.
🤝
You are not alone. You are not uniquely broken. You are human, and this is what loving and losing feels like.
Say this:
"Suffering is part of life. Other people feel this too. I am not alone."

📅 Intro — What is Relationship Timeline Reflection?

📅Narrative Therapy · Free
Relationship Timeline
Narrative Therapy · Free · ~20 min
Your story didn't begin with the ending. And it doesn't end there either.
Narrative therapy asks you to examine the story you are telling yourself about this relationship — because the story shapes how you heal. Most people, after a breakup, tell an incomplete story: one that is all loss, all failure, all pain.
What this session does:
Maps the full arc of the relationship — beginning, middle, turning point, end — so you can see it as a complete story rather than a wound. Then helps you identify patterns that may have been running beneath the surface.
A complete story has meaning. A wound just has pain.

🔍 Step 3 — Find the pattern beneath the pattern

← Breakup Recovery · Process
📅Narrative Therapy · Free
Relationship Timeline
Step 3 of 4 · The Pattern
This relationship may have been running a deeper script.
Tap any that feel true.
These are not judgements. They are patterns — and patterns can change. Seeing them is the first step.
Anxious Attachment
Needing constant reassurance. Fear of abandonment driving behaviour. Clinging harder when they pulled away.
Avoidant Dance
Attracted to emotionally unavailable people. Confusing unavailability with mystery or strength.
People-Pleasing
Shrinking yourself to keep the peace. Saying yes when you meant no. Losing yourself slowly.
Rescuer Pattern
Drawn to people who needed fixing. Your love as a project, not a partnership.
Repetition of Early Wound
This relationship echoed something from childhood — a parent, a dynamic, a familiar feeling of not being enough.
Fear of Intimacy
Pushing away when things got close. Sabotaging what felt too good. Safety in distance.

🔮 Intro — What is Memory Reconsolidation?
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🔮Ecker Protocol · Free
Memory Reconsolidation
Ecker Protocol · Free · ~25 min
Memories are not fixed recordings.
Every time you recall one, you can update it.
Memory reconsolidation is a neuroscience-based process developed by Bruce Ecker. When you recall a memory, it briefly becomes malleable — like wet clay. In that window, you can introduce new information that changes the emotional charge permanently.
This is not about forgetting.
The memory stays. But the emotional weight it carries — the gut-punch, the longing, the self-blame — can be reduced significantly. You update what the memory means, not what happened.
Research shows this works in as little as one session for some memories. It requires honesty and willingness to sit with discomfort briefly.

Step 1 of 5 · Find the Memory
Which memory carries the most emotional charge right now?
Not the memory you think you should work on. The one that actually shows up unbidden. The one that still hits.
It might be: the moment they ended it. A specific conversation. An image of them happy without you. The last good night before everything changed. A memory of feeling truly loved — and then losing it.
Describe the memory

🔍 Step 2 — Find the implicit belief
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🔮Ecker Protocol · Free
Memory Reconsolidation
Step 2 of 5 · The Hidden Belief
Every charged memory carries a hidden belief.
What does this memory tell you about yourself?
The emotional charge of a memory comes not from what happened — but from what the experience led you to believe about yourself or the world. This is the target.
Common hidden beliefs
"I am not lovable enough to stay." · "When people see the real me, they leave." · "I am too much." · "I am not enough." · "Love always ends in abandonment." · "I am fundamentally flawed."
When I sit with this memory, the belief it carries is...
This belief probably feels true right now. That is okay. You don't need to argue with it yet. Just name it clearly.

⚡ Step 3 — The mismatch experience
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🔮Ecker Protocol · Free
Memory Reconsolidation
Step 3 of 5 · The Mismatch
Now hold both truths at the same time.
This is the core of reconsolidation. You hold the old belief alongside new information that contradicts it. Your brain can't hold both simultaneously without updating.
The old belief (from the memory)
"I am not lovable enough to stay."
⟷
What you also know to be true
People who truly know you have chosen to stay, to love you, to come back. You have been genuinely loved. You are capable of deep connection. One ending does not define your worth.
Evidence that contradicts the old belief
Hold both at once. Feel the dissonance. That dissonance is the reconsolidation window opening.

🌊 Step 4 — Recall and update
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🔮Ecker Protocol · Free
Memory Reconsolidation
Step 4 of 5 · Update the Memory
Bring the memory back. Hold it. Then speak the new truth into it.
Close your eyes. Bring the target memory back clearly — the scene, the feeling. Let it be present. Now, while holding it, say the updated belief aloud:
Speak this aloud — slowly
"What happened was real and painful. AND — I am not defined by it. The belief I formed then was a response to pain, not a truth about my worth. I update it now."
Stay with the memory. Notice if the emotional charge has shifted — even slightly. Reconsolidation is rarely dramatic. It is often subtle at first, and deepens over days.
The updated belief I am choosing

🔄 Intro — What is a Thought Reset?
9:41●●●
← Breakup Recovery · Process
🔄CBT · Pattern Interrupt · Premium
✦ Premium
Thought Reset
CBT · Premium · ~15 min
The thought isn't the problem.
The loop is.
After a breakup, the mind runs the same painful thoughts on repeat — not because they are true, but because they are unresolved. A Thought Reset doesn't eliminate the thought. It interrupts the loop and installs a more accurate, grounded replacement.
Three steps:
1. Name the thought loop clearly
2. Interrupt it with a pattern break
3. Replace it with a calibrated reset phrase you actually believe
The replacement phrase must be true — not toxic positivity, not a lie. Just a more complete version of reality.

⚡ Step 2 — Interrupt the pattern
9:41●●●

🔄CBT · Pattern Interrupt · Premium
✦ Premium
Thought Reset
Step 2 of 3 · Pattern Interrupt
Break the loop before you can replace it.
A pattern interrupt creates a brief gap in the automatic loop — just long enough to insert something new. Choose one that works for you:
✋ Say STOP aloud
🧊 Hold ice for 5s
👋 Snap fingers 3x
💧 Splash cold water
🌬️ Exhale loudly
👀 Name 5 things you see
🦶 Stomp both feet
🎵 Hum one note
Do your chosen interrupt right now. Actually do it. The physical action is what creates the gap.

Thought Reset
Step 3 of 3 · The Reset
Write a reset phrase you actually believe.
Not "Everything is fine." Not toxic positivity. A reset phrase is more complete, more accurate, and more compassionate than the loop — but you must be able to believe it.
The loop says
A more complete truth is
Formula: "[The loop] is a real feeling. AND — [what is also true]."

Say your reset phrase aloud three times slowly after writing it.

Healing Ladder
Progress · Premium · Weekly
Healing is not linear. But it does move forward.
The Healing Ladder maps your journey across 10 stages — from acute crisis to renewed. Each week, check where you are. Over time, the movement becomes visible.
How to use this:
Be honest, not aspirational. Where you actually are — not where you think you should be. There is no wrong rung. Every rung is valid progress.
Most people move up 1–2 rungs per month with active healing work. Some weeks you move backward — that is also normal and expected.

✉️Journal · Expressive Writing · Premium
✦ Premium
Closure Letter
Journal · Premium · ~20 min
Say what was never said.
You don't have to send it.
Research by James Pennebaker shows that expressive writing about emotional experiences produces measurable improvements in mental and physical health — regardless of whether anyone reads it.
This letter is for you.
Not for them. Not to send. Not to get a response. To get the words out of your body and onto the page — because carrying unsaid things is heavy.
You will write in three parts: what happened and how it affected you, what you needed, and what you want to say now that it's over.

Meet Your Future Self
Positive Psychology · Free · ~20 min
You already exist in the future. Healed, whole, and free.
This is not wishful thinking. Research in positive psychology shows that vivid, embodied connection to your future self genuinely influences the choices you make today — and provides real relief from present pain.
What this session does:
Guides you to visualise, meet, and receive a message from your future self — 2 years from now, who has fully processed this relationship and built a life they love. You will speak to them. They will speak back.
The future self is not a fantasy. It is a real version of you — one who survived what you are going through right now.

🔄 Intro — Role Transition
9:41●●●
← Rebuild Identity
🔄ACT · Free
Role Transition
ACT · Free · ~15 min
You were a partner. That role is over. Something new needs to grow in its place.
ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) identifies role transition as one of the core challenges after a breakup. When a relationship ends, you don't just lose a person — you lose a version of yourself. The role of "partner", "future spouse", "person who belongs to someone" is gone.
The task is not to fill the void.
It is to consciously step out of the old role and intentionally step into a new one — not as who you were before the relationship, but as who you are becoming through it.

Step 1 of 3 · The Role You Are Leaving
Who were you in this relationship?
Be honest — not just the good parts.
The old role carried both gifts and costs. Some of it served you. Some of it didn't. Before you can step into the new, you need to fully see what you are stepping out of.
In this relationship, I was...
What you are losing from this role (tap all that apply)
Being chosen
Feeling needed
Shared future
A sense of home
Daily intimacy
Being known
Purpose through them
Feeling loved
Security
Identity as partner
Grief for a role is real — even when the relationship was unhealthy. You are allowed to miss what it gave you, while still knowing it is over.

📖 Intro — Write Your Story
9:41●●●
← Rebuild Identity
📖Narrative Therapy · Free
Write Your Story
Narrative Therapy · Free · ~20 min
You are the author of your story. Not the victim of it.
Narrative therapy, developed by Michael White and David Epston, holds that the stories we tell about our lives shape who we become. Most people leaving a relationship tell a story that positions them as a character things happen to. This session helps you reauthor that story.
The old story might be: "I was in a relationship. It ended. I am broken."

The reauthored story might be: "I am a person who loved deeply. That relationship was a chapter — not the whole book. The chapter taught me things. The story continues."

What story are you currently living inside?
Most people after a breakup are telling a problem-saturated story — one that positions the relationship as the defining event and themselves as diminished by it. Name it clearly before you rewrite it.
The story I have been telling myself is...
What role does this story give you?
The abandoned one
Someone left. You were not chosen. The story is about being unwanted.
The one who failed

The victim
Things were done to you. The story is about powerlessness.
The fool
You trusted and were hurt. The story is about your own naivety.

Write Your Story
Step 2 of 3 · The New Narrative
Rewrite from a different authorial position.
You are the protagonist — not the subject.
A reauthored story doesn't pretend the hard things didn't happen. It places them in a larger arc — one where you have agency, where the difficulty serves a purpose, and where the story continues beyond this chapter.
Narrative therapy prompts:
• What strengths did you show that the old story overlooks?
• What did this chapter teach you that you needed to learn?
• What would a compassionate biographer say about this period of your life?

Relationship Expectations
CBT · PREMIUM · ~20 MIN
Every relationship you enter, you bring invisible rules. This session makes them visible.
CBT research shows that unexamined relationship expectations are one of the primary drivers of recurring pain in love. We expect things we never name, get hurt when they aren't met, and never understand why.
What this session does:
Maps the expectations you brought into this relationship — where they came from, which were realistic, and which set you up for disappointment. You leave with clarity about what you actually need — not what you think you should want.

Relationship Expectations
STEP 3 OF 4 · CALIBRATION
Some expectations protect you. Some set you up for inevitable pain.
Not all expectations are unrealistic — some are healthy requirements. The question is: which are legitimate needs, and which were unfair burdens placed on another person?
Healthy: "I expect to be treated with respect."

Unrealistic: "I expect them to know what I need without me saying it."

Wound-driven: "I expect constant reassurance that they won't leave."
An expectation I held that was realistic and fair

Future Self Hypnotherapy
HYPNOTHERAPY · PREMIUM · ~25 MIN
A deep, guided journey to meet the version of you who made it through.
This session uses guided hypnotherapy — a clinically validated technique that uses deep relaxation and focused attention to access parts of the mind unavailable in ordinary waking state. You remain fully conscious throughout.
Before you begin:
Find a quiet space where you won't be disturbed. Sit or lie comfortably. Use headphones if possible. Follow each step slowly — do not rush. The 🔊 voice will read each step aloud.
Each step has a pause — stay with it before continuing.

Shifting Identity
SCHEMA THERAPY · PREMIUM · ~30 MIN
The beliefs that shaped how you loved are not permanent. They can be updated.
Schema therapy, developed by Jeffrey Young, identifies deep core beliefs — schemas — that form in childhood and silently govern how we behave in adult relationships. They feel like truth. They are patterns.
Common schemas in breakup pain:
"I am fundamentally unlovable." · "People always leave." · "I am too much." · "My needs don't matter." · "I must be perfect to deserve love."

These beliefs are not character traits. They are learned patterns — and learned patterns can be updated.

🔍 Step 1 — Identify your schema
9:41●●●
← Rebuild Identity
🧠Schema Therapy · ✦ Premium
✦ Premium
Shifting Identity
STEP 1 OF 4 · FIND YOUR SCHEMA
Which of these feels most true about you — even if you know it shouldn't?
These are the six most common schemas activated by relationship loss. Tap the one that resonates most — not the most logical, but the one that hits.
Abandonment
I will always be left. People I love inevitably disappear.
Defectiveness
There is something fundamentally wrong with me inside.
Emotional Deprivation
My emotional needs will never truly be met by anyone.
Subjugation
I must suppress my own needs to keep others from leaving.
Unrelenting Standards
I must achieve perfection or I have failed completely.
Self-Sacrifice
I give until nothing remains, and call it love.
The schema you find most uncomfortable to look at is usually the most active one.

⚡ Step 3 — Challenge and update
9:41●●●
← Rebuild Identity
🧠Schema Therapy · ✦ Premium
✦ Premium
Shifting Identity
STEP 3 OF 4 · THE UPDATE
The schema is a conclusion drawn from limited evidence. It can be updated.
Schema therapy doesn't eliminate schemas with positive thinking. It confronts them with contradicting evidence — moments and facts the schema has been filtering out.
The schema says: one thing.
Reality contains: evidence that contradicts it — evidence the schema has been systematically ignoring.
Evidence that contradicts my schema
A more complete, updated belief
The updated belief doesn't have to feel true yet. Write it anyway. The felt sense follows the cognitive update, not the other way around.

Shifting Identity
🧠✨
Schema Challenged
Schema change is not one session. It is a practice — returning again and again to challenge the old belief with new evidence. Each time, it loses a little more of its grip.
"My updated belief"
Your work going forward:
When the schema activates, notice it by name: "There's the abandonment schema again." Then read your updated belief. Over time, the new pathway gets stronger.
